static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with other runners tense due to self-criticism and constant comparison; has a supportive network of running companions, but has not yet fully shared feelings of inadequacy with them.
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness history; no prior psychological problems or treatment history.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic, highly cooperative, able to Reflect on one's 'should' phrasings and self-criticism; concrete emotional experiences (frustration, sadness, anger at oneself); speech rate Not mentioned.

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling inadequate and disappointed about marathon performance, believing oneself should win first place every time, but feeling too slow. These feelings appeared and intensified after a particularly grueling race last year, affecting training motivation and race performance, with self-criticism and discouragement appearing at every race.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I realize these feelings are affecting my enjoyment of running and hindering my performance; hoping to reduce self-criticism and re-enjoy running by identifying and restructuring 'should' phrasings.
growth_experiences: Last year experienced a particularly grueling and below-Anticipation race. After losing under high pressure (extremely high Demands on oneself), thoughts of 'I should win first place every time, I am too slow' and feelings of inadequacy began recurring. Since then training and race motivation decreased, overall performance declined, daily self-care affected; relationships with other runners tense due to self-criticism and constant comparison.

core_beliefs: Only if I get first place am I worthy / good enough
If I do not win, I am a loser
I am not good enough (too slow)

special_situations.event: Each time participating in a marathon without winning first place or performing below Anticipation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot win first place, it proves I am not good enough, unworthy of being called an excellent runner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increases training pressure, is harsh on the self, avoids sharing true feelings, maintaining a sense of worth through compulsive self-demands
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should come first every time; I am too slow

special_situations.event: When strong expectations about results and speed arise before or during a race
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching top speed and winning counts as success, otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on speed and ranking, ignoring the process and body signals; after the race, uses self-blame to 'spur' themselves
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot win this time, it means I am not good

special_situations.event: When seeing other runners' better results and rankings in training groups or on the course
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are stronger than me, it means I am bad, I am inferior
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing results with others, reducing expressions of vulnerability and help-seeking, proving oneself through extra training and self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them

special_situations.event: When recalling last year's poorly performed grueling race
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One loss can prove I am overall not good enough, making future goals hard to achieve
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Puts more energy into avoiding failure again rather than flexibly adjusting goals and process feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Not running well that time shows I am just not good

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen through victory, and to confirm self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated once failing, being at a disadvantage after comparison, thus feeling shame and worthlessness
defense_goal: Resisting the Anxiety of failure with strict self-Demands and perfect standards
Maintains control over the sense of worth through self-blame and inner harsh criticism

object_relations.self_representation: A competitor who must win to be recognized / otherwise a not-good-enough loser
object_relations.object_representation: Picky and judgmental others (peers, audience, or internalized judges)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked or talking about not yet winning first place, or being invited to relax the 'must win' standard
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' inquiries as negation of not trying hard enough or not being good enough (fearing judgment)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Focusing on one's own inadequacy in a self-blaming tone, ignoring external situational factors; frequently using 'should/must' in statements, lowering emotional expression, Reinforcement of self-criticism.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When noticing their emotions are running high (frustration, shame) and being invited to attend to feelings or meaning
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands emotions as risks that need to be controlled, tending to replace emotional contact with rules and goals
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Talking about performance and improvement in goal-, data-, and rule-based language, avoiding subjective emotional experiences and vulnerable expression.

manifestations: Takes victories and rankings as the sole source of self-worth; running changes from a passion into continuous 'performance evaluation'
Experiencing strong emptiness and frustration when not reaching first place, hard to derive meaning from the process and growth
outcomes: Decreased training and race motivation, reduced enjoyment
Negative emotions such as Anxiety and sadness recurring

manifestations: Bound by the rigid rule of 'should be first every time', finding it hard to flexibly set and adjust goals
Reduced sense of room for self-acceptance and choice
outcomes: Avoids experiencing vulnerability, limiting expression of real needs

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using self-Demanding statements like 'I should win first place every time' 'I should be faster'
Internalizes external judgments and win-lose rules as the sole standard of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Reviewing performance after races in a harsh self-critical way, emphasizing one's inadequacy to 'prevent mistakes'
When meeting setbacks, prioritizes blaming himself and reduces genuine emotional exchange with companions

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Turning pressure inward into self-blame and extra training when facing inadequacy, rather than seeking support from companions
Reduces sharing of vulnerable experiences, digesting more internally and engaging in self-criticism

positive_force: Having a supportive network of running companions (though not yet fully seeking help)
Willing to seek professional help and try new strategies (positive attitude)
Has proactively adjusted training and asked other runners for advice; has drive and willingness to improve
negative_force: Rigid 'should' rules and perfectionistic standards (equating winning/losing with self-worth)
Persistent self-criticism and low self-acceptance from comparing with others
Overgeneralizing one loss as overall inadequacy, triggering Decreased motivation and avoidance

antecedent: Focusing on speed and ranking before or during races
Race or training results below Anticipation
Seeing other runners' better results or rankings
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing winning as the sole value standard (not winning = not good enough), using self-blame as a means to drive change and avoid failure
target_behavior.function: Pursuing control and perfection through self-pressure, temporarily lowering Anxiety about 'failure/not good enough'
target_behavior.consequence: Frustration and sadness aggravated, decreased training and race motivation, Interpersonal tension, overall performance declining

target_behavior.behavior: Decreased training and race motivation (with avoidance tendencies)
antecedent: As a race approaches or when recalling last year's loss
When anticipating being unable to win first place
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white view of success/failure and Fear of shame (not winning means failure)
target_behavior.function: Briefly lowering Anxiety and shame by avoiding high-pressure situations
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced training volume, worsened process experience, Performance declining further and Reinforcement of Negative self-evaluation
